titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Adam to the Flood (ch. 2–8)
source: Carl Bezold, Kebra Nagast: Die Herrlichkeit der Könige (Munich, 1905), ch. 2–8 — public domain. Geʿez text as in Ran HaCohen's Unicode edition of Bezold (tau.ac.il/~hacohen/KN, from Michal Jerabek's 1995 digitization), archived and checked against Bezold's printed page. Per-sign transliteration derived mechanically from Unicode; word-level romanization auto-generated (schwa-reduced) and approximate. Transliteration convention: ś = ሠ-series, ʿ = ዐ-series, ə = 6th order, 1st order ä, 4th order a. Translations made fresh from the Geʿez; Dillmann's Lexicon (1865) the lexical aid.
about: Gregory, a worker of wonders imprisoned fifteen years in a pit, begins to ponder the greatness of kings. The account goes back to Adam, king of creation, and the envy of Cain and Abel; the line of kings from Seth to Noah; the sin of the sons of Cain; and the Flood.

sentences.l: Come-now let-us-return and-let-us-reckon and-let-us-weigh that-which we-make-greater and-we-make-less from-kings-of earth, in-law and-in-ordinance, in-glory and-in-greatness, from-first until last.
sentences.i: Come now, let us return and reckon, and weigh whom we should make greater and whom lesser among the kings of the earth, by law and ordinance, by glory and greatness, from the first to the last.
sentences.n: ሀቡኬ is ሀቡ, the plural exhortation 'come, come now' (the plural imperative of ሀበ 'give' used as an interjection; the same ሀቡ opens exhortations elsewhere in this work, e.g. ሀቡ ናንግሦ 'come, let us make him king'), with the enclitic ኬ 'now, then'. ንግባእ ወነሐስብ ወንወጥን are 1st plural subjunctives ('let us…') with ን-, joined by ወ-. ናዐቢ and ናሐጽጽ are causative (አ-stem) 1st plural forms, 'we make great' (አዕበየ, from ዐበየ) and 'we make less' (አሕጸጸ, from ሐጸጸ). ዘ- 'that which' is read here as 'whom/what'; እም- 'from' is partitive, 'among the kings of the earth'. The verb ንወጥን (ወጠነ) has 'begin, undertake, set about' as its primary senses in Dillmann; 'weigh, take in hand and consider' is my inference from context (at the end of ch. 2, አኀዝኩ እወጥን 'I began to ወጠነ' would be tautologous if it meant 'begin'), not a sense I can show from the lexicon. Nothing in the sentence is a crux, but the exact sense of the first clause is my reading of a compressed syntax. በ- 'in/by' marks the criteria (law, ordinance, glory, greatness). ነገሥተ is the construct plural of ንጉሥ. The ፨ sign closes the unit.

sentences.i: There arose Gregory, the worker of wonders, who was thrown into the pit for love of the witness of Christ, for fifteen years, in affliction;
sentences.n: Gregory (ጎርጎርዮስ) is the 'worker of wonders' of the Armenian church; the Armenian king in the next lines points to Gregory the Illuminator, who was held in a pit by King Tiridates. The identification is an inference from context; the text itself gives only the name and the epithet. ገባሬ መንክር 'worker-of wonder' is a construct. ዘተወድየ is ዘ- 'who' plus the passive (ተ-stem) of ወደየ 'put, cast'. ግብ 'pit'. ፍቅረ ስምዐ ክርስቶስ is a chain: love-of witness-of Christ; ስምዕ (witness, testimony) is also the word for martyrdom, so it means love of confessing Christ. ፲ወ፭ is 10 and 5, fifteen; ዓመተ 'years' stands in the accusative of duration.

sentences.l: While I-was in pit I-pondered concerning this matter and-concerning his-folly of-king-of Armenia, and-I-said, according-to my-thought, what (is) their-greatness: in-multitude-of army-ኑ? or in-glory-of goods-of world? or in-multitude-of appointment-of cities?
sentences.i: While I was in the pit I pondered this matter, and the madness of the king of Armenia, and I said, as far as my mind could judge: in what does their greatness lie? In the size of their armies? Or in the glory of worldly goods? Or in the number of governorships over cities?
sentences.n: እንዘ + perfect gives a circumstantial 'while I was' (እንዘ normally takes the imperfect; the perfect here is unusual, but the sense is plain). ሀለውኩ and ኀለይኩ are 1st singular perfects (ሀሎ 'be', ኀለየ 'ponder, think'). በእንተዝ 'concerning this'. በእንተ እበዱ ለንጉሠ አርማንያ is the Geʿez way of expressing a possessor after a suffixed noun: 'his madness, of the king of Armenia' (suffix -u anticipating ለ + owner). I read እበዱ as a noun 'folly, madness'; a 3rd plural perfect 'they were mad' is formally possible but the singular ንጉሥ fits the noun better. The allusion is presumably to King Tiridates' madness in the Gregory legend; that is an inference. መጠነ 'according to the measure of'. The enclitic -ኑ in ሰራዊትኑ marks a question, and ወሚመ is 'or'. ሢመተ አህጉር is 'appointment-of cities'; I take it as the offices or governorships given over cities; the exact sense of ሢመት here is not certain.

sentences.i: And this pondering of mine, at the close of each of my prayers, troubles my mind again, and I think about the greatness of kings, and I began to weigh it.
sentences.n: ለለ ተረፈ ጸሎትየ is uncertain. ለለ is a distributive 'each, every', and ተረፈ 'remainder' suggests 'in each remainder (the end) of my prayer'; the sense I give, 'at the close of each prayer', is a guess from context. የሀውከኒ is 'it troubles me' (3rd masc. imperfect ሀወከ with object suffix -ኒ 'me'). አኀዝኩ እወጥን is አኀዘ 'begin' plus an asyndetic subjunctive 'I began (that) I weigh'. The ፨ ፨ ፨ closes the paragraph, as in the source.

sentences.i: And I took up my thought from Adam, and said: God is in truth the King, to whom praise is due; and under Himself He appointed Adam king over all that He created;
sentences.n: አልዐልኩ is 'I raised, lifted up' (1st singular perfect, causative stem); the object is left unspoken, so 'my thought' is my supply, and the clause is uncertain. ዘሎቱ ይደሉ 'to whom it is fitting' (ይደሉ 'it is fitting, due'). ወእምታሕቴሁ 'and from beneath him': Adam's kingship is subordinate. ሤሞ is the perfect of ሠየመ 'appoint' with the object suffix -o 'him'; ለአዳም is the object restated with ለ-. ዘፈጠረ 'that which he created'. The idea: Adam as king of creation, Genesis 1:26-28 and Psalm 8, which is quoted in ch. 8.

sentences.l: And-in-his-transgression he-brought-out-him from-garden by-sin-of serpent, by-counsel-of devil; and-in that account-of sorrow was-born Cain;
sentences.i: And through his transgression he expelled him from the garden, by the sin of the serpent and the counsel of the Devil; and in that story of sorrow Cain was born;
sentences.n: Genesis 3: the expulsion from the garden (ገነት). ዕልወት is 'perversity, transgression'. አውፅኦ is አውፅአ 'he brought out' + -o 'him'. ኂጠተ is a spelling variant of ኀጢአተ 'sin' (accusative or construct); the chain ኂጠተ ከይሲ 'sin-of serpent' is a construct. The sense of ዜና ሐዘን 'account/news of sorrow' is loose; I take ዜና as 'story, affair'. Genesis 4:1 records Cain's birth.

sentences.i: And Adam saw Cain, his face set grim, wretched in his appearance, in sorrow; and again, Abel was born;
sentences.n: ርእዮ ... ለቃየን: the object suffix -o 'him' is repeated by the noun with ለ-, a regular doubling. እሱረ ገጽ 'bound-of face' (a passive participle in a construct) is an idiom for a grim or downcast face; ፀዋግ describes his look; elsewhere in this text it is used of a low, base fellow (ch. 76) and in a citation of Proverbs 6:12 of a worthless man, so I take it as 'wretched, base' rather than 'dark' (cf. Genesis 4:5, Cain's fallen face). The exact force here ('wretched', 'forbidding') is not certain. ወካዕበ 'and again'.

sentences.n: ዳግምሳ 'second' with the contrastive enclitic -ሳ. sentences.i: He was accursed, Cain, the killer of his brother; he multiplied evil, and his seed likewise, they who provoked God by their wickedness, and had no fear of God before their eyes; and they did not think of Him as their Creator, nor pray to Him, nor bow down, nor ask of Him, nor serve Him in fear;
sentences.n: ርጉም is 'cursed'; ቀታሌ እኁሁ 'killer-of his-brother' is a construct. አብዝኃ is the 3rd masc. perfect አብዝኀ with the 3rd fem. object suffix -ā, 'he multiplied it' (compare ይምልእዋ ለምድር), and ለእከይ restates the object, 'evil' (ለ- as an object marker). ዘርኡኒ: ዘርእ 'seed' with -u 'his' and -ኒ 'also'. እለ አምዕዕዎ 'who provoked him' (አምዐዐ 'to anger'). አልቦሙ 'they have not', 'they had no'. ፍርሀተ እግዚኣብሔር ቅድመ አዕይንቲሆሙ echoes Psalm 36:1 (35:2): 'there is no fear of God before their eyes'. The string of ኢ- negatives is a litany: ኀለየ (think), ጸለየ (pray), ተጋነየ (bow/serve), ሰአለ (ask), ተቀንየ (serve). ተጋነየ is 'bow down, prostrate'; later in this text it is paired with sacrifice and with asking and entreating.

sentences.i: They did nothing but eat and drink and dance and make merry to the lyre and in chants and in fornication, without law and without measure and without order; and the evils of the sons of Cain grew until, in the pride of their fornication, they brought the seed of the donkey to the horse, and there came to be a mule, a thing that God had not commanded;
sentences.n: ዘእንበለ ዘይበልዑ 'except that which they eat': 'apart from eating, drinking…' they did nothing else. መሰንቆ is a stringed instrument, 'lyre'; ማሕሌት 'chant' is a liturgical word, here applied to the sons of Cain's revels. ይትዋነዩ is 'they sport, make merry' (not simply 'sing'). CRUX: ዘርአ አድግ ኀበ ፈረስ 'the seed of an ass to a horse'. I read it as the breeding of donkeys with horses (mules), a mixing of kinds that God had not commanded, and the next unit compares it to believers marrying unbelievers. አግብአ (causative of ገብአ) with ኀበ 'bring to' is attested elsewhere in this work (አግብአቶሙ ኀበ ጽዮን 'she brought them to Zion'), so 'brought the seed of the ass to the horse' is the plain sense. በቅለ is 'a mule' (accusative, predicate of ኮነ), the offspring; I had first taken it as 'a sprout, a growth' from the verb, but the same word means 'mule' where it stands beside አድግ/ዓድግ elsewhere in the text. ዘኢአዘዘ 'which he did not command'. መስፈርት 'measure, restraint'.

sentences.n: CRUX: ዘርአ ግሙራ ርኩሳን. ግሙር is 'whole, complete', and ግሙራ stands as an adverb 'wholly, altogether' elsewhere in this work (አልቦ ዘይክል ጸሊአ ሥጋሁ ግሙራ), so I take it with ርኩሳን: 'altogether unclean'. That sits awkwardly with 'half of them good'; the likeliest sense is that even the good half is made unclean by the mixture, and the sentence may be compressed. My earlier guess 'mixed' has no support in the word. Uncertain. መሀይምናን 'believers' (plural of መሃይምን) and ከሓድያን 'unbelievers, apostates' (plural of ከሓዲ) are the two parties. እለ ይሁቡ is 'those who give' (relative ዘ plural + imperfect). መንፈቆሙ 'half of them' (መንፈቅ 'half' + -homu). The simile shows the sense of the donkey and horse image: the mingling of the chosen and the unchosen line.

sentences.i: Noah, however, was righteous: he feared God and kept righteousness, and the law that his fathers had told him, from Adam for ten generations; Noah himself remembered it and did good and kept his body from fornication, and admonished his sons not to be joined to the sons of Cain, who were conquerors, proud, and craving kingship;
sentences.n: Noah is described with the Genesis 6:9 phrase 'righteous'. ይፈርሆ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'he feared God' (object suffix and repeated ለ-); ዘነገርዎ አበዊሁ ሕገ 'what his fathers told him, the law' (ዘ + ነገርዎ with -o 'him', ሕገ in apposition). ዓሥር ትውልድ 'ten generations' is the span of Genesis 5 from Adam to Noah. ለሊሁ ኖሕ 'Noah himself'. እንዘ ይዜከር 'remembering' is a circumstantial clause (ዘከረ). ይጌሥጽ 'admonishes' (ገሠጸ). ከመ ኢይደመሩ 'that they not be joined' (ደመረ 'join'). The three epithets for the sons of Cain are uncertain. All three are singular in form, so they may belong to ቃየን himself or be distributive; I carry them over the sons. መማዕሊይ I read as 'conqueror' (perhaps from ሞዐ 'conquer'; the form is not secured), ዕቡይ is 'proud', and ናፋቄ መንግሥት 'longing for kingdom' (ናፋቄ is not in Dillmann as far as I can verify; the sense is from context).

sentences.n: CRUX: ዘይቈርር እምነ አስሐቲያ. ዘ- relative on ማየ አይኅ; ይቈርር is from ቈረረ 'be cold' (the root of አስቆረረ 'made loathsome' in ch. 4, and of ያቈርር መዐቶ እምኔነ 'he will draw back his anger from us' elsewhere in this work, where እም- also follows it); እምነ 'from'; አስሐቲያ is probably አስሐቲ (from አስሐተ 'lead astray') plus the feminine suffix -ā, 'her misleader' (the earth's; but the form is not secured, and the agent noun elsewhere is መስሕት). My reading 'which turn in loathing from the one who led her astray' is a guess; another possibility is that the water 'draws back from' or 'cools toward' them. I could not settle it. ደምሰሶሙ 'he destroyed them' (ደምሰሰ 'blot out', as in Cain's name being blotted out in ch. 4). The scene follows Genesis 7:11: ኀዋኅወ ሰማይ 'windows of heaven' is a construct; አስራብ 'torrents' (plural); አንቅዕት 'springs'; ተርኅወ and ተከሥተ are passives 'were opened', 'were uncovered'; ዘመትሕተ ምድር 'which (is) beneath the earth'.

sentences.l: For-his-sake they-were-created, and-for-his-sake they-perished, except 60 souls; and-from clean cattle and-beasts by-sevens; and-from unclean cattle and-beasts by-twos.
sentences.i: For his sake they were created, and for his sake they perished, except sixty souls; and from the clean cattle and beasts, by sevens; and from the unclean cattle and beasts, by twos.
sentences.n: በእንቲአሁ 'for his sake'. ዘእንበለ ፷ ነፍስ 'except 60 souls': the number is ፷ (sixty) in the source, although the passage clearly means those in the ark (Genesis 7:7, eight persons in all, cf. 1 Peter 3:20, which would be ፰); this may be a misreading in the digitization or a variant in the manuscript. I keep what the source gives. በበ፯፯ and በበ፪፪: በበ + a doubled numeral is distributive, 'seven by seven', 'two by two'; the clean animals are by sevens, the unclean by twos, as in Genesis 7:2-3 (whether sevens or seven pairs is not settled by this form). ንጹሕ 'clean', ርኩስ 'unclean'. The ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ run ends the part.
